Let me analyze the teaching examples more carefully to identify the correction rules.

Looking at Example 1 (2025-02-21):
- History: Prices have been dropping from 83.93 down to 72.67 over the last 18 days
- Model forecast: Starts at 74.49 on day 1, gradually decreasing to ~75.40 by day 18, then continues to 77.64 by day 30
- True outcome: Starts at 73.90 on day 1, gradually decreasing to ~70.11 by day 30

The model is consistently forecasting HIGHER prices than reality. The gap increases over time:
- Day 1-10: Gap is about +0.5 to +4
- Day 11-20: Gap is about +1 to +5
- Day 21-30: Gap is about +2 to +11

Looking at Example 2 (2025-02-20):
- Almost identical history (just shifted by 1 day)
- Model: Starts at 73.32, ends at 78.75
- True: Starts at 72.67, ends at 70.11
- Gap is also consistently positive (model > true)

Example 3 (2025-02-04):
- History: Prices have been dropping from 83.93 down to 72.67
- Model: Starts at 81.29, ends at 85.84
- True: Starts at 80.88, ends at 70.11
- Huge gap at day 30: +15.73

Example 4 (2025-02-03):
- Same history as Example 3
- Model: Starts at 81.38, ends at 83.46
- True: Starts at 80.96, ends at 70.11
- Gap at day 30: +13.25

Example 5 (2025-02-05):
- Same history


- Model: Starts at 81.49, ends at 79.66
- True: Starts at 81.12, ends at 70.11
- Gap at day 30: +8.55

I notice a consistent pattern of model forecasts being higher than true outcomes, with the divergence growing significantly over time. The gaps range from 3 to 15 units, suggesting a systematic bias in the original forecasting model.
